notes.text: Joel Eriksson Ek is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Maxim Tsyplakov has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. William Strömgren has taken his spot beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 16 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.

Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 3 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 36% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 38:37 together, down from 46% with Bahl.
William Strömgren was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 2% last season.

story.head: The Wild should tilt the ice
paras: The Flames won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in Calgary on Oct 22. The Flames (8-10-1) lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Nov 11, while the Wild have won two in a row. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (tied for first in the NHL) and the Flames sixth in the Pacific (tied for 25th).
The Wild’s record (.762) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.652), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Flames’ record (.447) is about what their chances are worth.

The Wild let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd), leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.19 goals a game, the fewest in the league. As for the Flames, they take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and take more penalties than they draw (31st). The Wild are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames. Beyond that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Kirill Kaprizov (17 G / 18 A / 35 P in 21 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is third in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (6 G / 22 A / 28 P in 21 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 19 GP) is next in line.

Jesper Wallstedt (13-2-3 / .925 SV% in 18 GS) has been a rock in net for Minnesota and will likely start. Devin Cooley (5-4-0 / .913 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for Calgary and will likely start.

At home, Ryan Huska likes to send Farabee, Backlund and Coronato out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy. Elsewhere, the Wild usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.
